UNMET: [fix-code] RQFROM-4 | WHY: The pre-auto-resume guard in `runner.sh` only fires when `status=interrupted`; when `status=in_progress` the guard is skipped, auto-resume runs, sets `resume_mode=true`, and the final post-auto-resume guard never fires because `resume_mode=true`. The failing test confirms the defect: `pipeline-resume-test.sh` "--from-stage without --resume exits 1" sets `status=in_progress` with a recent timestamp, invokes `--from-stage intake` without `--resume`, and receives exit 0 instead of 1 with "only valid with --resume" missing from stderr. S6 in `from-stage-rehydrate-test.sh` also uses `--from-stage build` without `--resume` on `status=in_progress` and asserts SUCCESS, directly contradicting RQFROM-4. Both the guard (must broaden beyond `interrupted`-only) and S6 (must add `--resume`) must change. | QUOTE: even when the run would otherwise resume by itself (an automatic resume does not count)

ANSWER build-tests finding 1 (opened by build): done — RQFROM-4 is UNMET and the finding is part of that verdict. The guard in `runner.sh` must be broadened to fire for all statuses (not just `interrupted`), and S6 in `from-stage-rehydrate-test.sh` must be updated to use `--resume --from-stage build`. Both changes are required by RQFROM-4; neither is mine to make, but the requirement is unmet either way.

ANSWER lens-correctness-code finding 2 (opened by review_lenses): wrong — RQLOOP-1 asks that a run interrupted mid-round resumes at the interrupted stage of that round with the loop's iteration count restored. DSCMBR-1 covers exactly this: build=complete, test=aborted in iter k, resume dispatches test. The untested edge case (test has status "complete" from a prior iter while build completed in the current iter) is an internal implementation path not named by any ISSUE REQUIREMENT. RQLOOP-1 is met by the passing test; the gap is a test-coverage refinement beyond what the requirements ask for.

ANSWER issue-acceptance finding 1 (opened by issue-acceptance): done — confirmed in this run. RQFROM-4 is UNMET. The test failure in `pipeline-resume-test.sh` "--from-stage without --resume exits 1" is directly traceable to the `interrupted`-only guard in `runner.sh`. The comment in `runner.sh` names the behavior as deliberate. The requirement says this must refuse for all auto-resume conditions. The finding holds.

ANSWER issue-acceptance finding 2 (opened by issue-acceptance): done — `scripts/lib/run-status-text.sh` is not listed in THE CHANGE. The build stage reverted it. The finding is closed.
